findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: An employee was observed to wash their hands and then not utilize a barrier to shut off the faucet, thus recontaminating their hands. This employee was educated on site about the importance of a barrier when handling the faucet to not recontaminate hands. Ensure employees are educated and trained on proepr hand washing techniques. 
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: At the start of the inspection there was a single sanitizer bucket observed made up with apparent soap film on top. The solution was tested and recorded at 0ppm chlorine. All other sanitizer buckets were observed dumped and not available. A new sanitizer bucket was created and tested at 100ppm chlorine. Ensure test strips are regularly used to ensure the efficacy of the sanitizer remains intact and ensure sanitizer buckets are readily available during all hours of operation. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on device and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: There is a visible gap present along the back entry door to the kitchen where substantial light is present where it is not protected from the entry of pests. Ensure that the back door receives maintenance to create a seal that does not allow for the visible light and lets the door seal completely, thus protecting the facility from the entry of pests. 
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: There is observed scattered debris present on the floor of the walk-in freezer. Ensure the debris is cleaned up to remove the current accumulation and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
6-501.12:  (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The walk-in cooler is observed still in disrepair during today’s spot check. Repairs are still in progress as the facility has had to order a specific part for the cooler before repairs can be made. For a temporary solution, a double door cooler has been placed in the main lobby area of the kitchen to allow for adequate cold holding space. An additional follow-up is being scheduled for February 7, 2024. 
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The walk-in cooler was observed operating at 51 degrees F during today’s inspection. PIC informed the inspector the walk-in cooler was down as of this morning. PIC and inspector temped items and determined the following items were not salvageable and the following items were voluntarily discarded during today’s inspection: All pre-cut lettuce bagged and prepped, Pea Salad, Individual Salad Cups, Baby Carrots, Anytime Snack Packs, Opened container of Ranch, Opened container of Mayo, Baked Potatoes, and prepackaged boiled eggs. 
Service calls have been made to have the cooler repaired, please see General Comments for additional details. Temperatures are taken of the cooler each morning and shall continue to be taken routinely each day to ensure proper cold holding temperatures of 41 degrees F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: There was observed a box of boiled eggs prepackaged and stored in the walk-in cooler. The eggs, out of temp, see violation #22, were observed with a best by date of 12-13-2023 and were voluntarily discarded during today’s inspection. Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. Ensure that food items are discarded if they exceed the use by date set by the manufacturer.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The mop sink is observed to have gaps on the upper edges of the mop sink basin. These gaps need to be sealed to prevent the accumulation of food debris and moisture from getting behind the edge barriers. Ensure a repair is made that creates a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: During the inspection, the mop was observed stored directly in the mop sink basin. The mop must be hung in a manner to allow for the air dry process to occur such as being hung by the handle on the mop holder or it may be stored in the top portion of the mop bucket where it is able to still air dry.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.114: During the inspection, the following equipment was observed non functioning:
-There is an oven with parts still on the top of the equipment needing to be repaired to make it functional.
-The right cold holding well in the lobby area is observed with parts still in the basin and in need of repairs to make the unit functional.
-The cold holding center display cooler is observed with an out of order sign on it. Ensure repairs are made to allow this equipment to properly function.
-Ensure repairs are made tot else items to allow them to be functioning properly for facility use. IF the equipment is unnecessary to the operation, then the unused equipment should be removed from the facility.  
6-501.114: The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: At the start of the inspection, there was a bottle observed with no label on it that was confirmed by staff to be bleach. The bottle has a label placed on it with a sharpie marker during the inspection. Ensure that working containers with sanitizers are properly labeled.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Facility PIC stated that Pest Control was recently present in the facility for their routine spraying. Observed today was two dead roaches on the floor near the dish machine. No live roaches were observed during today’s inspection. PIC was informed of these insects and was instructed to clean the harder to reach areas and the corners near the dish machine to get rid of the dead insects. Ensure regular cleaning is accomplished of these area to maintain them free of dead inspects/pests. 
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The fan by the dish machine is observed to have an accumulation of dust/residues blowing onto clean dishes. Facility shall clean the fan’s surfaces at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean.
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The bottom shelving of the dry storage is observed to have an accumulation of cobwebs/debris. Ensure these areas receive proper attention to detail when cleaning to remove the cobwebs and debris and then perform the cleaning practices at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-303.11: There is observed a lightbulb burnt out in the hood system above the ovens. Ensure once these surfaces have cooled that the lightbulb is replaced to allow for adequate lighting in this area. 
6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: The hand sink was observed to be out of paper towels at the start of the inspection. Paper towels were replaced in the dispenser. Ensure that hand sinks are supplied with proper items to be effective.  
6-401.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The fan used in the kitchen is observed to have an accumulation of dust/debris. This fan was removed from service and cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that items in the kitchen are maintained in a clean and sanitized manner.
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: There is observed older mouse droppings behind the dish machine area. PIC is aware and is instructing staff to clean the droppings. Extra precautionary glue traps are going to be placed to monitor the pests and to ensure that no active pest problem is taking place. Ensure that the facility is cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: Observed employee using a sanitizer rag to wipe their hands. This action was corrected on site by educating the employee on the proper use of a sanitizer rag. Ensure proper training is completed on how to properly utilize the sanitizer equipment and hand washing practices. 
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.15: Observed an employee using their gloved hands to handle the dirty dishes and then using the same gloves to handle the clean dishes. This action was corrected on site and education was provided to the employee on proper glove usage. Ensure proper training is completed on glove usage.
3-304.15: (A) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: As noted on 8/27/19 inspection, doors in stairwell off the kitchen have not been repaired to be tight sealing yet. A work order has been placed for this. Seal doors to prevent pest entry.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15  (C) Exterior door allows access for pests. Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. Reference 6-202.15.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
1) Doors in the stairwell off the kitchen are not tight sealing and there is approximately a 1/2 inch gap across under the two left doors and gaps in the corners of the two right doors. Seal doors tightly to prevent rodent entry. 

2) Observed mouse droppings on the floor under shelving units in the dry storage room and on the table underneath the dish machine. There are glue traps in these areas (dated 8/14) but no rodents have been captured as far as the person in charge is aware. Facility reports routine cleaning and sanitizing daily before food prep occurs. No evidence of pests getting into food at this time. Seal doors off kitchen and provide effective pest control to eliminate pests. Continue to clean and sanitize before food prep. Follow up 9/6/19.

6-202.15  (C) Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. Reference 6-202.15.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111  (Pf) The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate pests, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment: In the stairwell adjacent to the kitchen there are three large waste bins that are soiled inside and odorous. This may be contributing to the issue stated above. Clean receptacles or relocate to another area.
findings.citation_text: 5-502.11  (C) Waste receptacles and waste handling units were found overflowing with refuse and emitting objectionable odors. Refuse, recyclables and returnables shall be removed from the premises at a frequency that minimizes the development of objectionable odors and /or conditions that attract or harbor insects and rodents.  Reference 5-502.11.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed chicken strips in the reach in cooler (and a smaller batch in the prep cooler) that were reported to have been removed from cooking around 6:30 am and were observed wrapped (with condensation) and probed at 68F. Cooling logs are not available and it is unknown at what time chicken reached 70F, but it appears as though this did not occur in 2 hours since at almost 4 hours later it is 68F. Chicken strips were voluntarily discarded. Cooling methods for this type of item need to be discussed so that cooling can occur rapidly and food cool from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and to 41F or below within an additional 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15  (C) The method of cooling chicken is inadequate. Food must be uncovered during cooling, if protected from overhead contamination. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT-Hand sink was separating from the wall. Seal sink to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
